extracted.intended_audience: hospital finance officers, Medicare administrative contractors (MACs), hospital policy staff, health policy analysts, and other IPPS/LTCH stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and data rules CMS proposes to calculate the FY2027 inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS/LTCH PPS) outlier fixed-loss cost threshold, including how to incorporate outlier reconciliation, select and edit data (MedPAR, PSF, HCRIS), adjust CCRs, inflate charges, and include/exclude particular payments in the simulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-step methodology to incorporate outlier reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Identify hospital cost reports that meet the original criteria (Step 1a) or the new criteria (Step 1b). Step 2: Determine the aggregate amount of capital outlier reconciliation dollars (under both the original criteria (Step 2a) and the new criteria (Steps 2b)). Step 3: Calculate the aggregate amount of total capital Federal payments across all applicable hospitals using the cost report data. Step 4: Determine the percentage of total capital outlier reconciliation dollars to total capital Federal payments for the cost report data year. Step 5: Adjust the capital outlier adjustment factor using the percentage from Step 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cost report data, PSF, and HCRIS extracts to identify applicable cost reports; Steps 2–4 produce a percentage that is applied in Step 5 to adjust estimated capital outlier payments. (Refer to FY 2025 IPPS/LTCH final rule for complete step-by-step details.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of capital outlier reconciliation percentage (Step 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the aggregate amount from Step 2 (capital outlier reconciliation dollars under both the original criteria and the new criteria) by the amount from Step 3 (total Federal capital payments across all applicable hospitals using the cost report data) and multiply the resulting amount by 100 to produce the percentage of total capital outlier reconciliation dollars to total capital Federal payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round to the second digit when reporting; this percentage is then used in Step 5 to adjust the estimated percentage of capital outlier payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 5 adjustment: add/subtract reconciliation percentage
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Step 5 the amount from Step 4 is added to the estimated percentage of capital outlier payments otherwise determined using the shared outlier threshold. The analogous step for operating outlier payments subtracts the reconciliation percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the shared threshold is set using an operating target, do not adjust the threshold itself for capital—adjust the estimated capital outlier percentage by adding the reconciliation percentage. For operating, subtract the reconciliation percentage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of positive vs negative reconciliation dollars
rubrics_metrics.description: When the aggregate capital outlier reconciliation dollars in Step 2 is negative, the estimate of capital outlier payments is lower than the shared-threshold estimate, producing a relatively smaller outlier budget neutrality adjustment factor and an increase to the capital Federal rate. When the aggregate capital outlier reconciliation dollars are positive, the estimate is higher, producing a relatively larger budget neutrality adjustment factor and a decrease to the capital Federal rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative reconciled dollars indicate providers would owe Medicare at reconciliation, producing a negative percentage in Step 4 and thereby reducing the estimated capital outlier percentage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data choice for outlier reconciliation projection (hold-constant proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027 CMS proposes to hold the data constant and use the Step 4 percentage from the FY 2025 final rule (based on FY 2019 cost reports and PSF data) for both operating and capital outlier reconciliation projections rather than using the latest available data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is proposed because the most recent data (FY2021 cost reports) produced an anomalous 0.0 percent for operating reconciliation; aligning operating and capital projections to the same period (2019 cost reports) minimizes distortions from differing reporting periods and preserves comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulation approach to calculate proposed outlier fixed-loss cost threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulate payments by applying proposed FY 2027 payment rates and policies to cases from the FY 2025 MedPAR file; differences from actual claim payment inputs (e.g., CCRs and charges) are handled by using adjusted CCRs and inflating MedPAR charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the simulation formula in section I.C.1 of the Addendum; the simulation produces an outlier threshold that targets a specified percentage of total payments (including outlier reconciliation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge inflation factor methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a 1‑year average annual rate-of-change in charges per case using two most recent Federal fiscal year periods of MedPAR charge data, and apply that 1‑year rate twice to inflate MedPAR charges by 2 years (to go from FY2025 data to FY2027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027 CMS used December 2024 MedPAR (FY 2024) and December 2025 MedPAR (FY 2025) to compute the rate; for the final rule CMS would use newer MedPAR files (March 2025 and March 2026). This approach balances use of recent CMS data and stakeholders' ability to replicate the factor using publicly available Federal fiscal year MedPAR files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion rules for hospitals when computing charge inflation factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Include hospitals whose last four digits fall between 0001 and 0899, include CAHs and REHs that were IPPS hospitals for the MedPAR data period, include hospitals in Maryland, and remove PPS-excluded cancer hospitals identified by a 'V' in the fifth position of their provider number or an 'E'/'F' in the sixth position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also include providers that are present in both periods of charge data used to calculate the 1‑year average annual rate-of-change. This is consistent with methodology used since FY 2014.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure Medicare FFS claims only in MedPAR sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Include claims with a 'Claim Type' of 60 (field indicates FFS claim) and exclude claims with 'GHOPAID' indicator of 1 (indicates a claim is not FFS and is paid by a Group Health Organization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the simulation captures only fee-for-service claims when estimating charge inflation and outlier payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of specific paid items from covered charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove pharmacy charges for anti-hemophilic blood factor (indicator '3' and revenue code '0636') and organ acquisition charges from the covered charge field because these are paid separately under IPPS; propose to remove allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition charges for budget neutrality adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements are excluded because they are paid outside the IPPS bundled payment and would distort covered charge-based cost estimates used in outlier threshold calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and adjustment of CCRs from Provider-Specific File (PSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: For projection, use CCRs from the December 2025 PSF update and apply edits/adjustments to model the outlier threshold: search for IHS providers and providers assigned the statewide average CCR and replace/assign the upcoming fiscal year's statewide average CCR; assign statewide average CCR to providers with missing CCR or whose CCRs exceed ceilings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply subsequent adjustment factors to hospitals assigned the statewide average CCR. Also apply an adjustment factor to CCRs to account for cost and charge inflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR adjustment factor methodology (national average case-weighted comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust CCRs by comparing the national average case-weighted operating and capital CCR from the most recent PSF update to the national average case-weighted CCR from the same period of the prior year, using the same case count on both sides of the comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CMS computed December 2024 operating national average case-weighted CCR of 0.24059 and December 2025 of 0.235176, producing a one-year operating CCR adjustment factor of 0.977497; similarly, capital CCR adjustment factor example was 0.951277.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR ceiling and statewide average assignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §412.84, calculate CCR ceilings and assign a statewide average CCR for hospitals whose CCRs exceed 3.0 standard deviations from the mean of the log distribution of CCRs for all hospitals. Specifically, if MAC computes operating CCRs > 1.278 or capital CCRs > 0.13, or if MAC cannot compute a CCR, statewide averages are used to determine outlier qualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables (8A, 8B, 8C) list proposed statewide average CCRs for urban/rural hospitals and LTCH total CCRs; statewide averages effective for discharges on or after Oct 1, 2026, and replace prior year statewide ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not apply CCR adjustment factors to hospitals assigned statewide average CCR
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals that are assigned the statewide average CCR are not subject to the additional adjustment factors that CMS applies to CCRs to account for cost/charge inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents double-adjusting CCRs for hospitals where only the statewide average is used; hospitals assigned statewide averages may work with their MAC to request alternative CCRs per the Claims Processing Manual guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and alternative CCR process guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS encourages hospitals assigned the statewide average operating and/or capital CCRs to work with their MAC on a possible alternative operating and/or capital CCR as explained in the Medicare Claims Processing Manual (section 20.1.2 of chapter 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of an alternative CCR developed jointly with the MAC can avoid overpayments/underpayments at cost report settlement and may obviate the need for outlier reconciliation; hospitals may request an alternative CCR at any time following manual guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index and related policy inclusions for payment estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: For outlier threshold estimation use a wage index that reflects proposed policies including rural and imputed floor adjustments, State frontier floor adjustments under ACA section 10324(a), proposed out-migration adjustment (section 505 of Public Law 108-173), a 5-percent cap on any decrease to a hospital's wage index from the prior FY, and continuation of the transition for discontinuation of the low wage index hospital policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of these wage index policies ensures total FY2027 payments are estimated correctly; omitting them would bias the outlier threshold and the target percentage of outlier payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude Hospital VBP and Readmissions adjustments from outlier calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include hospital VBP payment adjustments and hospital readmissions payment adjustments in the proposed outlier threshold calculation or the proposed outlier offset to the standardized amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlier payments are calculated based on the unadjusted base DRG payment amount consistent with definitions under §§412.152 and 412.160; including these adjustments would be inconsistent with statutory and prior CMS interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include estimated per-discharge uncompensated care payments allocated equally
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate an estimated per-discharge uncompensated care payment amount to all cases for hospitals eligible for the uncompensated care payment when calculating the outlier fixed-loss cost threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes allocating per-discharge payments equally best approximates estimated uncompensated care payments and provides predictability for hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include estimated supplemental payments for eligible IHS/Tribal and Puerto Rico hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Include estimated per-discharge supplemental payments to hospitals eligible for supplemental payments (IHS/Tribal hospitals and Puerto Rico hospitals) in the computation of the proposed FY2027 outlier fixed-loss cost threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These supplemental payments are included consistently with methodology finalized in FY2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting outlier threshold to account for reconciliation (FY2027 example)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to incorporate a projection of outlier reconciliation dollars by targeting an outlier threshold at 5.14 percent [5.1 percent - (-0.04 percent)] for FY2027, reflecting the incorporation of projected outlier reconciliation into the determination of the outlier threshold. This yielded a proposed threshold add-on of $51,704 for FY2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reconciliation were not applied, the proposed threshold would be $52,096. CMS used the ratio from the FY2025 final rule (based on FY2019 cost reports) to compute the reconciliation adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply outlier adjustment factors after removing prior-year effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the proposed outlier adjustment factors to the FY2027 payment rates after removing the effects of the FY2026 outlier adjustment factors on the standardized amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the proposed adjustments are applied on a consistent, prospective basis rather than layering on previous adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy against retroactive aggregate adjustments to outlier payments
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will not make retroactive adjustments to outlier payments to force actual outlier payments to equal the prospective target (e.g., 5.1 percent) because doing so would undermine the prospective nature and predictability of the IPPS and would contravene statutory language indicating outlier payments are to be projected/estimated (not actual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A retroactive, across-the-board adjustment would alter payments for all hospitals and remove the ability to approximate patient payment while hospitalized; see FY2003 Outlier final rule rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR numeric examples / thresholds used in methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Example computed values: December 2024 operating national average case-weighted CCR = 0.24059; December 2025 operating = 0.235176; resulting one-year operating CCR adjustment factor = 0.977497. For capital: Dec 2024 = 0.01644; Dec 2025 = 0.015639; one-year capital CCR adjustment factor = 0.951277.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses these computed adjustment factors to modify PSF CCRs for the projection; include total transfer-adjusted cases from FY2025 to determine national average case-weighted CCRs for both sides of the comparison so case count is identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan to reassess data for final rule and invite public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: For the FY2027 final rule CMS plans to evaluate updated data available at the time of final rule development (e.g., March 2026 HCRIS extract of FY2021 cost report) to determine whether anomalies persist and whether to use that updated data; CMS is inviting public comment on the proposed methodology for incorporating capital outlier reconciliation payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on evaluation results, CMS may consider updated data for the final projection rather than the held-constant FY2019-based approach.
